area_summary:
The in-game HUD is almost entirely J2DScreen .blo layouts. d_meter alone owns six screens (main_parts1/2/3.blo, choice_road.blo, time_swim_1/2.blo). They draw through the Painter's single J2DOrthoGraph, whose virtual box is x -9..650, y -21..503 (constants @5162 0x803F7D68 = -9 and @5163 0x803F7D6C = 650, loaded by mDoGph_Painter at 0x8000B03C/4C and 0x8000BA00/10). The Gecko code widens exactly that box to -123..767, so its global 2D compression is the same as the anamorphic model.

I extracted the vanilla .blo files from the user's CISO into scratch and parsed them, so every position below comes from real pane rectangles. The decomp code moves nearly every HUD pane relative to its fopMsgM_pane_class::mPosCenterOrig/mPosTopLeftOrig. fopMsgM_pane_parts_set copies those from the J2DPane bounds once, right after J2DScreen::set. That gives one cheap, shared choke point: shift the root-level panes' bounds by ±S between J2DScreen::set and the caller's fopMsgM_setPaneData. Everything derived from Orig then follows with no other code changes: the clock and swim-sparkle dDlst_2Dm_c rectangles, the rupee and arrow 2D particles, the minimap D-pad hints, and the Gecko's special cases (rupyInit, clockMultiMove, swimTekariScroll, magicTransNowInit, heartScaleInit, compassDirOpen).

The cleanest way to get that choke point for every screen in the game, REL screens included, is two hook_branchlink sites inside J2DScreen::set(const char*, JKRArchive*) at 0x802D0944, with an anchor table keyed by .blo file name. S = 329.5*(F-1) ortho units (109.83, rounded to 110, for 16:9), because the ortho half-width is 329.5 about c = 320.5.

Cheap data-only parts:
- The minimap position: g_meter_mapHIO, read every frame.
- The timer's rupee offset: g_menuHIO+0x9A.
- Vtable-slot swaps for one-off dDlst draws.

Code parts:
- The anchor pass (T2, about 0x150-0x1C0 bytes, because dMeter_Create runs at every stage load, possibly before the REL's 300-frame gate).
- A calcScissor wrapper (about 0x60 bytes).
- One shared mDoLib_project wrapper, hooked at the six HUD call sites that place 2D at a projected 3D point: x' = 320 + (x-320)*F.

Expensive or per-element parts are few: the cannon-game battery (vtable wrapper), the mgameboard minigame numbers (positions live in a stub REL), the telescope side fills, and the operate-wind full-screen mask. The Z-target cursor is a 3D model and needs nothing. Centred UI needs nothing: boss HP bar, choice arrows, baton UI, wind-selector circle, 3-2-1-GO starter, minigame timer bar.

items.what: Shared anchor pass: shift the root-level panes of a J2DScreen left/right by S right after the .blo is loaded, before the caller copies pane positions into fopMsgM_pane_class (all later moves are Orig-relative)
items.where: JSystem/J2DGraph/J2DScreen.cpp:23-32 J2DScreen::set(const char*,JKRArchive*); f_op/f_op_msg_mng.cpp:9791-9805 fopMsgM_pane_parts_set (copies pane->getBounds() into mPosTopLeftOrig/mPosCenterOrig); f_op/f_op_msg_mng.cpp:9850 fopMsgM_paneTrans (= Orig + delta)
items.dol: J2DScreen::set(name,arc) 0x802D0944 (size 0xE8). Hook A: 0x802D0968 `bl 0x802B68F0` (JKRFileLoader::getGlbResource(name=r3, arc=r4)); the name is NOT kept in a saved register. Hook B: 0x802D09DC `bl 0x802D0CE0` (J2DScreen::set(JSURandomInputStream*), r3=this from r29, r4=&stream), returns bool in r3, followed by `mr r31,r3` at 0x802D09E0. Helpers: J2DScreen::search(u32) 0x802D1150, J2DPane::add(f32,f32) 0x802D05C8 (calls move 0x802D054C, then calcMtx). J2DPane layout: mTag +0x08, mBounds +0x0C (i.x,i.y,f.x,f.y), mPaneTree (JSUTree) +0xB0. First child link = *(pane+0xB0); link->mObject +0x0 = child J2DPane*; link->mNext +0x0C. Each HUD .blo has a full-screen PAN1 tagged 'ROOT' under the screen; the HUD panes are ROOT's children.
items.assumption: Pane rectangles in the .blo files are authored for a 640x480 layout with the 4:3 ortho box -9..650; fopMsgM_pane_parts_set snapshots them once.
items.effect_native: After the global 2D compression every HUD element is confined to the centre 4:3 region; nothing reaches the screen edges.
items.anchor: per screen rule (see the hud-meter-* items): L = -S, R = +S, C = 0, F = expand about the centre (x0' = 320.5 + (x0-320.5)*F, w' = w*F) for full-width panes
items.gecko: No equivalent. The Gecko moves things per function instead: J2DScreen::draw x offsets, paneTrans wrappers at -114, and direct mMtx[0][3] pokes. Six of its dMeter patches exist only because it shifts the current position instead of Orig; this pass makes all six unnecessary.

open_questions: Global 2D compression method: my S = 329.5*(F-1) assumes the global-2D area widens the Painter's box (@5162/@5163) symmetrically about 320.5. If it compresses some other way, S = vanilla left edge (-9) minus the new left edge. Settle this with that area before coding.

Mode toggles mid-stage: the anchor pass runs when a J2DScreen is created (dMeter at each stage load, timers on demand). After a toggle the HUD stays compressed-but-unanchored until the next stage load. The map/menuHIO writes and vtable swaps take effect at once. Is that acceptable, or should C also re-walk the live meter panes and adjust the fopMsgM_pane_class Orig fields (more code)?

T2 budget: the anchor pass, calcScissor wrapper and project wrapper total roughly 0x250-0x300 bytes of T2 on top of the culling hook (0xBF8 free before it). If that's too much, the project and battery wrappers can live in the REL through mailbox function pointers (they only matter in gameplay, after the 300-frame gate). The anchor pass should stay in T2, because the first stage's dMeter_Create can run before the REL links.
Pause-menu L/R hints ('l'/'r' in main_parts1) and the item-to-button flight (item_parts, d_meter.cpp:6240-6280) depend on whether the menus area keeps pause-menu pages centred 4:3. I assumed it does.
Sploosh Kaboom (d_a_mgameboard) number positions live in a stub-only REL; check a screenshot live before deciding.

The HUD margin: preserving vanilla edge distances puts hearts and buttons about 33 ortho units from the 16:9 edge, which may sit in TV overscan on real displays (not in Dolphin). A configurable inset (S_eff = S - inset) is trivial if wanted.

The J2DScreen::set hooks change behaviour for every screen in the game, so the table must default to 'no change' for unknown names (strcmp miss → return). Confirm the menus and overlays areas want to share this choke point, and agree one table format.

Dolphin check: confirm live that with view->mAspect widened, 'Force 16:9' + Widescreen Hack OFF gives the anamorphic stretch the HUD numbers assume, and that the hack's heuristic doesn't kick in (culling plan §9).
